page: OVHcloud r3-512 is a memory-optimized server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 20 Gbps baseline bandwidth alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier multi-core performance, with the stress-ng multi-core test and PassMark CPU score both placing in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 8439.52 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 296.1 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, perform at average levels, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches top-tier speeds of 813.47 GB/sec.

This instance is designed for memory-intensive workloads that require high resource density and strong multi-threaded execution. It demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, achieving 134.58 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and scoring in the top 25% for PassMark database operations. While the 400 GB NVMe SSD provides fast local storage, its capacity is relatively small compared to the 512.0 GB RAM, suggesting a tradeoff where large datasets must be managed externally or fit within memory. The high core-to-memory ratio offers qualitative cost efficiency for in-memory databases, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference.
